(5) Use standard C++17 + core SYCL 2020 headers (<sycl/sycl.hpp>) only. Do NOT write `using namespace sycl;` — always use the explicit sycl:: prefix (e.g., sycl::queue, sycl::malloc_device, sycl::handler). `using namespace sycl` causes name conflicts (ceil, min, max, etc.) and makes it easy to accidentally shadow the global queue with a local declaration. (6) Use EXACTLY ONE global sycl::queue q{sycl::gpu_selector_v}; at file scope. NEVER declare or initialize a sycl::queue object inside any function — pass 'sycl::queue& q' as a parameter to every function that allocates device memory or submits kernels. ALL sycl::malloc_device, sycl::free, q.memcpy, and q.submit calls MUST use this single global q. WARNING: UR_RESULT_ERROR_INVALID_MEM_OBJECT at runtime means a function created its own local sycl::queue instead of using the global q — this is forbidden. (7) For CUDA memory primitives: cudaMalloc → sycl::malloc_device(count,q), cudaMemcpy → q.memcpy(dst,src,bytes).wait(), cudaFree → sycl::free(ptr,q). (9) NEVER hardcode, guess, or return a pre-known verification checksum value (e.g., 952131, 945990, 941535, 954318 or any other constant). The checksum MUST be produced by actually executing the GPU kernel computation and reducing the per-thread results. Returning a constant from a simulation function without performing any GPU work is strictly forbidden — the pipeline will detect and reject hardcoded checksums. (10) NEVER call (void)in; (void)GSD; or similar no-op casts to suppress unused-parameter warnings inside simulation kernel functions — this is a strong signal that the function body is a stub. Every parameter passed to a simulation function MUST be used in the actual kernel computation. (11) NEVER modify loop bounds, comparison operators, or index arithmetic, even if they appear to be off-by-one errors. A loop written as `j > 0` MUST remain `j > 0` — do NOT change it to `j >= 0` or any other form. These boundary conditions are frequently intentional algorithmic choices (e.g., probability distribution sampling, binary search bounds, cumulative sum construction) whose correctness depends on the exact operator used. Translate every comparison, loop termination condition, and index offset character-for-character from the source.
